CLEAN PASS WITH CAVEATS. 60 rows = 12 items x resp 1..5; validate_items.R --table-sets passes both sets exactly. (1) SOURCE AND CODE DERIVATION: data/yang_2023_green_brand.py lists the literal strings 'A1','A2','A3','B1','B2','B3','C1','C2','C4','D1','D2','D3' in its SCALES dict and melts them with var_name='item', so the IRW item code IS the S1 File's column name -- no positional step, no rename. The S1 File is a plain CSV whose header carries bare codes and no wording at any level (no variable or value labels exist in a CSV), so mapping_basis is paper_explicit, not data_labels: the words come from the paper's Table 1, which prints each item beside the very code the data uses. NOTE the item wording was read from the JATS manuscript XML (article/file?id=...&type=manuscript), which carries Table 1 as real markup -- NOT OCR from the table image. The batch_234 sibling transcribed the same table from the PNG; the two transcriptions agree character for character on the four items they share, which is a useful cross-check on that OCR. (2) THE C3/C4 DEFECT, and it is the main finding here. The paper's Table 1 and Table 3 both print the third social-image item as C3; the S1 File has no C3 column and has C4 instead. This was settled against the data, not assumed: Cronbach's alpha for {C1,C2,C4} is 0.71195 against Table 3's published 0.712 for the three-item 'Social Image of Agribusiness' factor, and no two-column subset comes near it ({C1,C2}=0.575, {C1,C4}=0.607, {C2,C4}=0.677), so the published three-item factor cannot be two of these columns plus an unobserved C3. C4 therefore carries the wording Table 1 prints against C3 ('The company often holds public welfare activities.'), which is what ships. (3) BLOCK IDENTITY: recomputing alpha per letter block on the S1 File reproduces all six of Table 3's published alphas to 3dp (A .807/.80748, B .779/.77891, C .712/.71195, D .743/.74331, F .849/.84915, E .934/.93354; largest deviation .00048), so the four blocks shipped here are the four brand-image dimensions and not one of the sibling scales. Within-block order rests on Table 1's explicit code labels -- see verify_yang_2023_green_brand_image.R; PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. (4) LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: administered in Chinese (341 consumers of green agricultural products, 32 Chinese provincial capitals, Nov 2022-Jan 2023). No Chinese wording exists in scope -- the article has exactly ONE supplementary file, the S1 CSV, and it is pure ASCII with zero CJK characters; there is no questionnaire supplement. So the 2026-09-01 fallback applies: the study's own English from Table 1 in the base fields, the four _translated columns empty, language=Chinese, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. (5) DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM VERBATIM, both disclosed: the source's typographic apostrophes (U+2019 in "the brand's") were normalised to ASCII, matching the rest of itemtables/ (no shipped __items.csv uses U+2019); the source's own inconsistent terminal punctuation was NOT normalised -- A2, B1, B2, B3 and C1 end without a full stop in Table 1 and end without one here. (6) OPTION TEXT: only the endpoints are labelled anywhere in the paper -- 'scored on a 5-point Likert scale, with the numbers 1-5 representing the level of agreement ... That is, 1 means "disagree," and 5 means "agree".' So resp 1='disagree', resp 5='agree' and resp 2/3/4 are BLANK rather than padded with their own numbers. These are the paper's English methods-section gloss of the administered Chinese anchors, and that axis is not independently verified. (7) instructions and section_prompt are blank: the paper never quotes an instruction stem addressed to respondents, and none was invented. section_id is the trivial yang_2023_green_brand_image_1 -- the scale's four dimensions are subscales, not shared-context testlets, so they were not made into section_ids; the dimension membership is recoverable from the item-code letter (A=Agribusiness image, B=Agricultural product image, C=Social image of agribusiness, D=Consumer image). correct_response blank throughout (attitude scale, no key). The items are the study's own composite, built by the authors from Biel, Aaker, Parasuraman and Sun Rui et al. rather than reproducing any named publisher instrument, and they are printed in full in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article ('This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited'). STEP 5b -- ORCHESTRATOR RE-CHECK OF THE ROUND'S OWN CLAIMS. All three agent claims that override a source or would become a public artifact were independently reproduced by the orchestrator, and all three CONFIRM. (1) THE E/F TABLE-NAME SWAP. Recomputed per-letter-block Cronbach's alpha directly from the S1 CSV: A=0.80748, B=0.77891, C=0.71195, D=0.74331, E=0.93354, F=0.84915 (n=341 each). Read Table 1 and Table 3 out of the JATS manuscript XML as MARKUP, not OCR: both assign E1-E3 to 'Consumption intention' (published alpha 0.934) and F1-F4 to 'Customer perceived value' (published alpha 0.849). E matches consumption intention to -0.0005 and misses perceived value by 0.085. CONFIRMED: IRW's yang_2023_perceived_value and yang_2023_consumption_intent are swapped relative to the source. Two agents reached this independently in this round and a third did in batch_234. (2) THE C3/C4 DEFECT. The S1 CSV header is literally [...C1, C2, C4...] -- there is no C3 column. alpha{C1,C2,C4}=0.71195 against Table 3's published 0.712 for the three-item Social Image factor. CONFIRMED. (3) THE UPPS-P ANCHOR OVERRIDE, the one claim in this round that contradicts its source outright. Reproduced from the S1 workbook: negative urgency {6,8,13,15} r=+0.537 with the study's own CES-D total, positive urgency {3,10,17,20} r=+0.479, (lack of) premeditation {2,5,12,19} r=-0.074, sensation seeking r=+0.322, perseverance r=+0.014 (n=494); raw 20-item alpha 0.8337 vs published 0.834; raw 20-item sum correlates r=1.000000 with the workbook's own SUPPSP total, confirming the live table stores UNREVERSED responses. The negative-urgency items are worded in the impulsive direction, so under the paper's printed '1 (strongly agree) to 4 (strongly disagree)' a higher score would mean LESS impulsivity and the correlation with depression would have to be negative. It is +0.537. CONFIRMED: the printed anchors are transposed and the agent was right to ship the reverse. Also verified the UPPSP_1 header truncation directly -- column 47's header ends '...according to your actual situation.-1. I', so the item label really is destroyed to a single letter. (4) A CORRECTION OWED TO AN EARLIER BATCH: batch_234's provenance for the sibling records Table 1 as image-only on the grounds that grep over the scraped article page returns 0 hits for 'E1'. That is true of the article PAGE but false of the source -- the manuscript XML carries Tables 1 and 3 as real markup. batch_234's OCR transcription is corroborated character-for-character, so nothing it shipped is wrong; only its provenance note's account of the route is.
